q: According to Newton's second law, an object that is accelerating must have a _____ acting on it.
e: An object that is accelerating must have a net force acting on it according to Newton's second law.

q: An object moving in a circle must have a force applied to it to keep it moving in the circle, and this force is known as the _____.
e: The force applied to an object to keep it moving in a circle is known as the centripetal force.

q: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal acceleration which is directed towards the _____ of the circle at any moment.
e: Centripetal acceleration is directed towards the centre of the circle at any moment.

q: In the absence of centripetal force, the object would not move along a circle but move in a _____, according to Newton's first law.
e: According to Newton's first law, in the absence of centripetal force, the object would move in a straight line.

q: When whirling a body attached to a string, the _____ force behaves as a centripetal force.
e: The tension force in the string behaves as a centripetal force when whirling a body.

q: An attractive force exists between the sun and the earth in a direction _____ to the path of the earth.
e: The gravitational attractive force between the sun and the earth acts in a direction perpendicular to the path of the earth.

q: The _____ attractive force between the nucleus and the electron acts as the required centripetal force.
e: The Coulomb attractive force between the nucleus and the electron acts as the required centripetal force.

q: When a car turns in a circular path, the _____ force acts normally to the direction of motion of the car.
e: The frictional force acts normally to the direction of motion of the car when it turns in a circular path.

q: When a car moves in a circular path which is inclined to the horizontal, the _____ component of normal force is the required centripetal force.
e: The horizontal component of the normal force is the required centripetal force on an inclined path.

q: The upward thrust (lifting force) acts normally to an aeroplane body; when it tilts, the horizontal component provides the _____ force.
e: The horizontal component of the lifting force provides the centripetal force when the aeroplane tilts.

q: On a flat road (unbanked road), the centripetal force is supplied by _____ between the tires and the road.
e: On an unbanked road, the centripetal force is supplied by friction between the tires and the road.

q: If the frictional force is not sufficient, such as under wet and slippery conditions, the car will _____ out of the circular path.
e: If frictional force is insufficient under wet conditions, the car will skid out of the circular path.

q: Banking of roads is raising the _____ edge of the curved road higher than the inner edge.
e: Banking of roads involves raising the outer edge of the curved road higher than the inner edge.

q: The angle that the inclined track makes with horizontal is called the angle of _____.
e: The angle that the inclined track makes with the horizontal is defined as the angle of banking.

q: For every banked curve, there is a limiting speed at which the entire centripetal force is supplied by the horizontal component of the _____ force.
e: At the limiting speed, the entire centripetal force is supplied by the horizontal component of the normal force.

q: At the limiting speed on a banked curve, the _____ force between the tires and the road is not required.
e: At the limiting speed on a banked curve, the frictional force between the tires and the road is not required.

q: Since there is no vertical motion on a banked road, the net force on the car in the y direction is _____.
e: Since there is no vertical motion, the net force on the car in the y direction is zero.
